seoTitle: Free JSON to .env Converter - Flatten Config Online
metaDescription: Flatten JSON config into KEY=VALUE lines with upper-case names joined by underscores. Handles arrays and quoting. Free and runs in your browser.
intro: Flattens a JSON config into .env lines, joining nested keys with underscores in upper case, so database.host becomes DATABASE_HOST.
why: Configuration often starts life as a JSON file and then has to become environment variables for Docker, a CI job or a hosting dashboard. Retyping nested keys as flat names is easy to get wrong, and values with spaces or a dollar sign need quoting rules that vary between loaders. This tool walks the JSON, builds the names for you and quotes values that need it. You can add a prefix, change the separator, switch off upper-casing and choose how arrays are written. It runs locally, which is useful because config files tend to hold passwords and tokens you would rather not paste into a stranger's server.
howTo: Paste a JSON object into the input box. The top level has to be an object.
Set an optional prefix and separator, and choose upper-case keys or not.
Pick how arrays are written: indexed keys, one comma-separated value or a JSON string, then copy the result.

faq.a: The path is joined with your separator (underscore by default), characters outside A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and underscore are replaced by underscores, and the result is upper-cased unless you turn that off. So app.port becomes APP_PORT.
Indexed mode gives KEY_0, KEY_1 and so on. Comma mode joins simple values into one line. JSON mode stores the whole array as a JSON string. Comma mode falls back to JSON when an array holds objects.

Empty values and anything containing whitespace, #, quotes, $, backticks, backslashes or = are wrapped in double quotes with the special characters escaped. Plain values stay bare. null becomes an empty value.

faq.q: Will every .env loader read the output?
faq.a: Most will, but quoting rules differ slightly between dotenv, Docker and shells. Test the file with the loader you actually use before relying on it.

keywords: convert json config to environment variables
